reasoning: ت for ث and ishi for thing are Palestinian. It means most of all (aktar ishi b7ibbo); 'the most important' would be ahamm ishi.

meaning_fix: futile effort / going round in circles achieving nothing (lit. pounding water, it stays water)
reasoning: The idiom (fuller form: da'' il-mayy w hiyye mayy) describes pointless work that changes nothing, not evasive speech. Shadda on ق gives '' in da''.
Taa marbuta is a after ر and e after ن. kharbaan is the everyday word for broken.

yoom with oo. The scheme writes the glottal after the article; in fast speech it is il-a7ad or il-7add.
Quadriliteral participle with the reduced m- prefix and a glottal ق.

kahraba (electricity) is Palestinian. The broom word has variants (mukinse, maknase); in construct it becomes -et. Vowelling uncertain.
Palestinian word for pears, with the first vowel dropped and an emphatic S.
